units: <cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 7:5">Yoma VII, 5</cite> <he>כהן גדול מְשַׁמֵּשׁ וכ׳</he> the high priest officiates in eight garments, and the common priests in four. Y. ib. 44ᵇ bot. <he>מפני מה אינו משמש וכ׳</he> why does he not officiate (on the Day of Atonement) dressed in gold? <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 21:9">Lev. R. s. 21</cite> <he>מקדש ראשון ע״י שׁשִׁמְּשׁוּ בו וכ׳</he> during the first Temple, because they ministered in faithfulness, only eighteen high priests officiated in it.
<cite ref="Yoma 47a:13">Yoma 47ᵃ</cite> <he>ש׳ תחתיו</he> officiated in his place.
<cite ref="Yoma 47a:13">Ib.</cite> <he>וכולן שמשו בכהונה וכ׳</he> and all of them performed the functions of high priesthood.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 9:10:2">Y. Sot. IX, 24ᵃ</cite> <he>אלו שימשו פרנסות</he> the former served in an administrative capacity (not merely as scholars). Tanḥ. Bo 4 <he>חשך ואפלה שמשו</he> … <he>ולא עתידין לשַׁמֵּשׁ</he> ‘darkness and mist’ served (as divine agents) in Egypt, but ‘void and waste’ never served, and never shall serve; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 360">Yalk. Is. 360</cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 33">Gen. R. s. 33</cite>, end <he>לא שמשו מזלות וכ׳</he> the planets did not perform their functions during all the twelve months (of the flood); <he>שמשו אלא … ניכר</he> they did act, only that their mark was not recognizable.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 3:8:3">Y. Yoma III, 41ᵃ</cite> top <he>חמשה … הסגן משמש</he> the Sagan had five functions to perform.
<cite ref="Mishnah Tamid 5:5">Tam. V, 5</cite> <he>שלשה … מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת</he> it served three purposes.

Midd. I, 6 ומה היו מְשַׁמְּשׁוֹת and what were they used for? R. Hash. 3ᵃ כי משמש וכ׳ ki serves for four meanings &c., v. דִּילְמָא I; a. fr.—Euphem. ש׳ מטתו, or only ש׳ to perform the marital duty; in gen. to couple (also of animals).
<cite ref="Niddah 17a">Nidd. 17ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Niddah 2:1">Ib. II, 1</cite>.
<cite ref="Bekhorot 8a">Bekh. 8ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 20">Gen. R. s. 20</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Mikvaot 8:4">Mikv. VIII, 4</cite> <he>שִׁמְּשָׁה את ביתה</he>, v. <cite ref="B00753"><he>בַּיִת</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 2:1">Ned. II, 1</cite> <he>קונם שאיני מְשַׁמְּשָׁךְ</he> I vow that I will not have intercourse with thee.
<cite ref="Nedarim 15b">Ib. 15ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Ketubot 71b:4">Keth. 71ᵇ</cite> <he>מְשַׁמַּשְׁתּוֹ</he> she must allow him marital intercourse; a. fr.

senses.gloss: (denom. of שַׁמָּשׁ) to attend, serve, wait upon.
units: <cite ref="Pirkei Avot 1:3">Ab. I, 3</cite> <he>המְשַׁמְּשִׁין את הרב</he>, v. <cite ref="P00015"><he>עֶבֶד</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 32b:6">Sabb. 32ᵇ</cite> <he>זוכה ומשמשין לו וכ׳</he> he will live to see himself waited upon by two thousand … servants.
Kidd. 32ᵇ מצינו גדול ממנו שש׳ we find that a greater man than he waited (upon his guests); Yalk. Ex. 229; a. fr.—Esp. (of students) to be in attendance upon a scholar as a disciple.
Ber. 47ᵇ אפי׳ … ולא ש׳ תלמידי וכ׳ even if one has studied the Bible and the Mishnah, but has failed to wait upon scholars, he is considered an ʿam haarets (v. אֶרֶץ).
<cite ref="Sotah 47b:22">Sot. 47ᵇ</cite> <he>שלא שִׁימְּשׁוּ כל צורכן</he> who did not wait upon scholars sufficiently.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 10:5:2">Y. Sabb. X, 12ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>שִׁמַּשְׁתִּי את אבא וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="J00689"><he>יְשִׁיבָה</he></cite> Ib. III, 6ᵃ (in Chald. dict.) <he>ולא שי׳</he>, v. <cite ref="O00046"><he>סָבוֹרָא</he></cite>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: (with ב) to be handled, be used for; (of persons) to make use of, be waited upon.
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 48b:4">Snh. 48ᵇ</cite> <he>נ׳ בהן קודש אסור להִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בהן חול</he> having once been used for a sacred purpose, it is forbidden to use them for a secular purpose.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 84b:13">B. Mets. 84ᵇ</cite> <he>כלי שנ׳ … יִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בו חול</he> shall a vessel that has been used for a sacred purpose, be used for a profane purpose (i.e. shall I marry one inferior to my first husband)? <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 119">Midr. Till. to Ps. CXIX, 134</cite> <he>כלי שנ׳ בו מלך וכ׳</he> a vessel which the king has used &c., v. <cite ref="O00154"><he>סָגָן</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Chullin 60b:2">Ḥull. 60ᵇ</cite> <he>שׁיִשְׁתַּמְּשׁוּ בכתר אחד</he>, v. <cite ref="K01388"><he>כֶּתֶר</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 2:5">Koh. R. to II, 5</cite> <he>ברוחות</he> … <he>מִשְׁתַּמֵשׁ וכ׳</he> Solomon made use of the spirits, and he sent to India &c.
<cite ref="Berakhot 52b:19">Ber. 52ᵇ</cite> <he>אסור להשתמש בשמש וכ׳</he> you must not be waited upon by an ignorant waiter.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 37">Gen. R. s. 37</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 62:18">Yalk. ib. 62</cite> <he>שהיו מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁין ברוה״ק</he> (not <he>משמשין</he>) who made use of (acted under) holy inspiration; a. fr.
